title: Keyboard manager does not disable hotkeys when they are "rolled"

status.label: Maintainer-owned work is in progress
status.detail: A maintainer reproduced disabled Win+E/Win+V shortcuts leaking through when keys are rolled; the issue remains assigned and labeled In progress.

judgment.rationale: A maintainer reproduced the exact rolled-key failure, and the live issue remains assigned to gokcekantarci with Status-In progress. This is active upstream ownership; parallel fix work would duplicate the assigned investigation.
evidence: The issue describes disabled Win+E and Win+V shortcuts firing when the user rolls from one key to the other while holding Win.
A second user reproduced both key orders on PowerToys 0.59.0.
A maintainer explicitly said they could reproduce the behavior.
The live issue is assigned to gokcekantarci and retains the Status-In progress label.
PR #32125 is mentioned in a comment about separate issue #10393; it is closed without a merge timestamp and is not evidence that this issue was fixed.
judgment.recommended_action: Leave the rolled-shortcut investigation with its current assignee and do not start competing fix work.

fix_assessment.rationale: The same reproducible issue is actively assigned and labeled In progress. No competing fix proposal should be created while the maintainer-owned work remains active.

issue_context.summary: Disabled Win+E and Win+V remaps reportedly leak through when their keys are pressed in overlapping or rolled order while Win is held.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.58.0 and Win+E/Win+V disabled remaps.
A second user reproduced the issue on 0.59.0 and a maintainer confirmed reproduction.
The issue is currently assigned to gokcekantarci and labeled Status-In progress.
inferences: The assigned maintainer may already be investigating shortcut overlap or key-state transitions; no implementation details are available in the public discussion.
issue_context.analysis: The active assignee and in-progress status are sufficient to avoid parallel implementation. The comment referencing PR #32125 concerns a separate issue and does not establish coverage for this rolled-key behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all four comments, including the user reproduction and maintainer confirmation.
Checked the live assignee and labels.
Verified PR #32125 is closed without being merged and that its discussion concerns #10393 rather than this issue.
